identity.real_world_identity_notes: Fiat Uno prepared for the Brazilian Copa Uno one-make series, which began in 1992 under Greco Competicoes with official Fiat support. It was built on the Uno 1.6R with a 1,600 cc engine prepared by the organiser and drawn by lot each round.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The reviewed reference lists a sequential stick and the cockpit shows an H-pattern lever. The observation is preferred and was deliberately re-checked: the same driver identified a sequential stick on the Chevrolet Montana in the same session, so the two were being told apart rather than defaulted, and the absence of automatic cut and blip fits a road-derived H-pattern gearbox rather than a racing sequential. The same reference also overstates the ARC Camaro gear count.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. Construction is inferred from a one-make series using the production Uno gearbox rather than stated by a source.
Recorded independently of Uno Classic B, the Copa Classic B division car. They are separate selectable identities and neither inherits from the other.

The earlier record cited a community site generated from Coanda's AMS2 spreadsheet, which describes the simulator rather than the real car. That reference also listed a sequential gearbox, which the drive contradicted: the driver confirmed an H-pattern lever on a second look.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.copa-uno.20260814t192029139z-97984302 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the shifter was confirmed by a second cockpit inspection after a reviewed source disagreed.

claims.basis: A registered reference establishes the car and its output, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The registered history establishes the series and its Fiat Uno 1.6R base but says nothing about the gearbox. The five H-pattern gears come from the live drive, and synchromesh is the ordinary reading of a road-derived manual rather than a stated specification.
